Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

remain verb

stay, not leave

also stay, stay behind, stay put, stay on, remain behind

classical

Plaut. As. 597: quīn tū hīc manēs?
Cic. Att. 8.3.7: in Ītaliā fortasse manēbitur (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 370, 385

maneō, manēre, mānsī, mānsum

verb, second conjugation

stay, remain

Of staying where one is: at home, in a place, with someone (apud aliquem). With an adjective, of staying in a state: clausae fenestrae manent, the shutters stay shut (Plin. Ep. 9.36.1). The imperative manē is “wait!”.

Other words

  • remaneō, remanēre, remānsī — stay behind

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.14.3: mulierēs nostrae praeter cēterās Rōmae remānsērunt

    Of those who stay when others leave.

  • commoror, commorārī, commorātus sum — stay on, stay for a while

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.20: diūtius ibi commorābimur; Traupman 104

    Cicero’s word for stopping somewhere on a journey, or staying longer than planned.

  • permaneō, permanēre, permānsī, permānsum — stay to the end; last

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 22: modo permaneat studium et industria

    Of what lasts or holds out.

Examples

  • Quō nunc abīs? quīn tū hīc manēs?

    Where are you off to now? Why don’t you stay here?Plaut. As. 597

  • signifer, statue signum; hīc manēbimus optimē

    standard-bearer, plant the standard: this is the best place for us to stayLiv. 5.55.2

  • clausae fenestrae manent

    the shutters stay closedPlin. Ep. 9.36.1

See also remain, wait, come back soon.
